basis: Visual estimate from panels-b-adventurous.png against panels-b-2045.png. Percentages for ground refer to developed foreground parcels, not the central agrivoltaic field.

roofMix.reading: Foreground terraces carry almost whole-roof PV, with planted roofs on taller corner blocks. The distant existing town remains a grey and clay pitched-roof field. Vertical agrivoltaics are not counted as roof area.

wallMaterials.material: honey timber frame on taller blocks

windowRhythm.storeyHeightMetres: 2.9 to 3.1 on terraces; 3.2 to 3.4 on corner blocks
windowRhythm.windowWidthMetres: 0.9 to 1.2 on terraces; 1.8 to 2.2 within a 3 m bay on blocks
windowRhythm.windowProportion: Terrace windows about 0.55 to 0.70 width:height; block glazing about 1.2 to 1.5 width:height
windowRhythm.revealDepthImpression: Moderate on homes at 180 to 250 mm; deep on timber blocks at about 350 mm.
windowRhythm.rhythm: One or two tall openings per dwelling bay, clear party breaks, and a stronger regular timber bay on the corner blocks.

groundCover.reading: Foreground courts and streets are planted and inhabited. Beyond them, the separate agrivoltaic field remains predominantly grazed grass, not hard landscape.

water.visible: Several small wetland ponds and a narrow connected channel along the right side of the agrivoltaic fields. Existing treatment tanks remain circular engineered objects.
water.pondSize: Shallow irregular ponds roughly 18 to 40 m across
water.reflectivity: Mid-value silver-blue, #88A4A8 lit and #304C50 shaded, with high reed cover and only 35 to 50 per cent open reflective surface.
water.buildability: The number and exact shapes of board ponds are partly invented. Keep water within mapped wetland or drainage areas and prioritise two or three readable surfaces.

trees.density: High in the flanking woodland and orchard, low within the grazed panel rows, medium around foreground homes.
trees.arrangement: Disciplined orchard rows, clumped woodland belts with irregular edges, street avenues, and sparse wetland trees that do not hide the panel field.

sustainableFeatures.PVGlint: Roof and field panels are blue-black #17252F with thin pale blue-grey edge glints #91A5AD. Keep grazing green visible so the central field does not become a black slab.
sustainableFeatures.canopies: Minor in the foreground. Any parking canopy must remain visibly elevated on slim posts.
sustainableFeatures.agrivoltaicRows: The focal feature: vertical bifacial panels about 2 m high, single thin rows at about 10 to 12 m centres, aligned with the field grain. At least 80 per cent of each field remains visually green. Sheep read as small cream dots between rows.
sustainableFeatures.glasshouses: A compact distant group near the top centre, clear or pale blue-grey roofs with fine white frames. They should read as agricultural glass, not opaque sheds.
sustainableFeatures.other: Wetland ponds, orchard production and the retained water-treatment works complete the productive-landscape reading.

people/vehicles.people: Tiny figures in the foreground courts and a few farm workers between panel rows. The board's sheep are stronger scale cues than people in the central field.
people/vehicles.vehicles: Sparse cars on foreground streets, service vehicles near glasshouses, no parking scattered through pasture.
people/vehicles.scopeNote: Sheep and workers are not worth full geometry at this range. If retained, use a few instanced low-detail markers after the panel rows and shadows are correct.

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate shows dark stripes painted on the ground; the board shows individual vertical bifacial rows with height, gaps, posts, shadow and grazing beneath.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Replace the agrivoltaic land-cover stripe with instanced vertical 2 m panel rows at about 11 m centres, following terrain and field axes, and cast narrow shadows.
gapsVsPlate.system: scripts/golden_valley_2045.py data and futureGeometry in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate woodland is a carpet of identical angular crowns; the board has deep, varied belts, orchard rows and readable open edges.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Deploy separate woodland, orchard, avenue and veteran forms, with clumped density and a darker interior grade.
gapsVsPlate.system: tree geometry/grade in landcover.js and future.js, plus gv-2045-trees.bin generation

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate's foreground roofs and walls are almost black and beige blocks; the board resolves whole-roof PV, warm brick and planted corner-block roofs.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Increase residential PV coverage, reveal module seams and tune home/corner-block materials separately using the approved warm brick and timber palette.
gapsVsPlate.system: roof shader and facade materials in facades.js, with futureGeometry in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate glasshouses are pale opaque boxes; the board has fine-framed transparent-looking agricultural volumes.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Keep opaque rendering for robustness but add fine roof/wall frame lines, brighter sky-facing panes and darker lower reflections so the volumes read as glasshouses.
gapsVsPlate.system: glasshouse branch in futureGeometry and facades.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: Water in the plate is a flat colour and partly disappears; the board has reflective ponds and a connected wetland edge.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Strengthen two or three mapped ponds, use sky reflection at low roughness and soften their reed margins into the wet meadow.
gapsVsPlate.system: ground shader in future.js and water treatment in life.js
gapsVsPlate.effort: 0.5 to 1 day, covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate field is one uniform olive plane; the board shows grazed pasture, panel-row wear, sheep and changing meadow texture.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Add low-frequency grass variation and a restrained lighter strip beneath panel rows. Do not model individual blades or every sheep.
gapsVsPlate.system: gv-2045 land-cover data and ground shader in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board adds picturesque ponds and shifts distant development and woodland boundaries relative to the plate.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Reject the drift. Keep mapped field, water and building boundaries, borrowing only the vertical-panel construction and material character.
gapsVsPlate.system: geometry and data lock, no model change
